title: The Spy in the Shanghai Office
synopsis: At night, someone uses the secret list.
Kim Gu, the police chief, needs clues.
goal: Find out who copied the secret list, prove it to Kim Gu, and stop the copy.

notes: A time worked out from Haesu's note: the light went on at eleven; half of a four-hour candle burned, two hours; the light went out at one in the night, 01:00.
Haesu, the candle and the light are made up.

learning.objective: at eleven, burns for four hours, half of it was gone을 읽고 불이 꺼진 시각(01:00)을 계산한다.
expressions: A new candle burns for four hours.
This morning, half of it was gone.

play.title: Half a Candle
story: A young clerk drops a note.
It is in Hangeul. No name.
play.letter:
Detective, someone used the list desk last night.
At eleven, the guard saw the light go on.
I left a new candle there. A new candle burns for four hours.
This morning, half of it was gone.
Half of four hours is two hours.
— a friend in this office
play.question: When did the light go out? Use four numbers, like 07:00.
hints: The light went on at eleven. How many hours did half the candle burn?
Half of four hours is two. Eleven, twelve, one.
play.successMessage: The light went out at one in the night!
transition: Someone was there, eleven to one.
"I am Haesu. I wrote that note."

feedback.1300: It was night, not the afternoon. One in the night is 01:00.
feedback.2300: Eleven is when the light went ON. When did it go out?
feedback.1100: Eleven is when the light went ON. When did it go out?

play.orderFeedback: Right numbers, wrong order. Hours first.

notes: Played as a search (InvestigationScene with a picture file): the police report's three lines say where each thing is (next to, on, under); the thin paper, with names pressed into it, shows the list was copied.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheet of government_office.webp (picture.measuredOn): the list desk in the middle with the thin paper drawn under it, the window and its sill (the ink bottle drawn on it) on the right, the iron stove lower right with the key drawn beside it, the door on the left, the bookshelf behind the desk; each find's place is where the picture draws it; no two areas overlap.
The police report is made up; that the police bureau watched for spies is history (h3).
2026-11-11: played as a picture choice (key, ink, thin paper), not a search: the search found all three and answered by itself, so the child never chose.

play.letter:
The key is next to the stove. It opens the list desk.
The ink bottle is on the window sill. It is normal office ink.
The thin paper is under the list desk. Names are pressed into it.
— Kim Gu's police
play.question: What shows the list was copied?
hints: The report says where things are.
play.successMessage: Names are pressed in. The list was copied!
transition: Someone wrote a copy on top.
His pen pressed the names in.

clue.value: THIN PAPER · NAMES PRESSED INTO IT

evidence.name: The Police Bureau's Report

evidence.inscription: The thin paper is under the list desk.

notes: The sign-out book (listed out of time order): only one clerk left after the light went out at one (Mission 1); the guard has no office key. The clerks and the book are made up.

clueInputs.note: The light went out at one in the night.

play.title: The Sign-Out Book
story: A sign-out book hangs by the door.
Each clerk writes when they go home.
play.letter:
Mr. Seo: left at half past eleven.
Mr. Nam Giho: left at a quarter past one.
Haesu: left at nine.
Mr. Pak: left at ten.
The night guard: at the front door all night. He has no office key.
Your clue: the light went out at one.
play.question: Who was here when the light went out? Type his name.
hints: See your first clue for the time.
A quarter past one is after one.
play.successMessage: Only Mr. Nam Giho was here at one!
transition: Mr. Nam Giho is new here.
His desk is empty this morning.
Haesu runs to tell Kim Gu.

lines.text: Only clerks have a key at night.
So a late clerk made the copy.

discovery.title: THE NEW CLERK
discovery.detail: Mr. Nam Giho stayed until a quarter past one. Now tell the police chief.

notes: Mr. Nam's three claims, each refuted by one mission's evidence picked from three cards: nobody at the desk (Haesu's note: the light from eleven to one), nothing copied (the police report: names pressed into thin paper), home at nine (the sign-out book: a quarter past one). Then his coat is searched and the copy found: the answer 'copy_found'.
Kim Gu is real; every word he says is made up (dossier fiction), resting on h1-h3. The spy, the list and the clerks are made up.

clueInputs.note: The light burned from eleven until one.
The list was copied onto thin paper.
Mr. Nam Giho left at a quarter past one.

learning.objective: 남기호의 세 주장(Nobody was at the list desk / Nothing was copied / I went home at nine)을 읽고, 각 주장이 틀렸음을 보여 주는 증거 카드를 고른다.

play.title: The Police Chief
story: "Mr. Nam says he did nothing. Show me clues."
play.letter:
Nobody was at the list desk last night.
Nothing was copied.
I went home at nine.
play.question: Show where Mr. Nam is wrong.
hints: Each thing Mr. Nam says is wrong. One card shows it.
Desk: Haesu's Note. Copy: police report. Nine: sign-out book.
transition: Sewn inside Mr. Nam's coat is the copied list. It never left Shanghai.
Kim Gu locks it all away.
play.orderFeedback: One card for each thing Mr. Nam says.

evidence.name: Kim Gu's Case Note
evidence.description: The copied list was found sewn in Mr. Nam's coat. It never left Shanghai. Haesu's note, the thin paper and the sign-out book proved it.

interview.speaker: kim_gu
interview.goal: Show Kim Gu that Mr. Nam is wrong.

He says nobody was at the desk.
He says he went home at nine.

lines.text: It began after the March First Movement.
I became police chief in August 1919.
At first, I only asked to be the door guard.

play.caseSummary: A light burned from eleven to one. Thin paper showed a copy. Mr. Nam Giho left last. The copy was in his coat. Kim Gu was the police chief. In 1940, he became the leader.

notes: PART 10 Case 09; PART 1A (2026-11-09): an independent case. Haesu, a young clerk, warns the detective with an unsigned note (a spy may be in the office). PART 3 (2026-11-09): the guard has no office key; the final refutes Mr. Nam's three claims and the copy is found in his coat.

Kim Gu is real; his words are made up (dossier fiction). The spy Nam Giho, the list, the clerks, the candle and the police report are made up. The case ends on history: the Provisional Government founded in Shanghai in April 1919 and Kim Gu's police (h1-h3).
